title: Printed relaxor polymer dielectric hitting k near 60
idea: Magnify dielectric constant by slot-die coating P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) relaxor terpolymer (k~50-60) biased in its non-switching paraelectric regime as a planar storage capacitor dielectric.
why: Capacitor charge wall: Fact 1 needs k~70 to escape the pillar; a printed planar capacitor with k~60 approaches it at ~1/10 the process cost.

title: Octopus arm ganglia: in-tier decoders built in the same channel film
idea: Octopus arms carry their own ganglia; in a 3D stack, form a small oxide-TFT decoder in each tier from the same channel film and the same slit/hole patterning as the cells, so each tier needs only ~log2(N) shared address lines instead of N individually contacted wordlines.
why: Per-tier contacts, staircases and CMOS drivers stop growing with tier count, so 120+ tiers (~10x bits/mm2) can be built without the periphery (49% of the die) and contact cost scaling up (facts 2, 7).

title: Periphery outsourced to idle 28 nm logic wafers, bonded under array
idea: Po: half the chip is missing. Existing DRAM fabs make array-only wafers (cells, bitlines, minimal local sense) while idle 28-40 nm logic fabs make periphery wafers (decoders, sense amps, I/O); the two are hybrid-bonded wafer-to-wafer with periphery under the array.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): ~1.6-1.9x more bits per existing DRAM wafer start using surplus mature logic capacity; no new fab.

title: Idle Gen-8.5 display fabs make glass-panel memory
idea: Worse: limit DRAM to round 300 mm wafers while LCD fabs sit idle. Flip: convert surplus Gen-8.5 display lines (2.2x2.5 m glass, ~70x a wafer's area) to make oxide-TFT gain-cell memory panels with their existing steppers and sputter/PECVD tools, then dice them into tiles for capacity-tier modules.
why: Capital: ~$1-2B conversion versus $15B+ for a new fab; panel area offsets ~10-20x lower density; no crucible quartz, no EUV.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor anodizing grows self-ordered 100:1 storage holes
idea: Borrowed from aluminum electrolytic capacitor foils and AAO filters, which self-organize hexagonal pores with AR >1000 just by anodizing aluminum in acid. Deposit thick Al over the cell array, seed pores on the landing-pad lattice by shallow pre-patterning, anodize straight down to any depth, then ALD electrode and dielectric into the alumina template.
why: Facts 1/4: the high-AR capacitor etch is the costliest array step; anodizing is a room-temperature wet bath with no plasma tool and no aspect-ratio-dependent etch slowdown. Pore ordering at <40 nm pitch is the risk.

title: Capacitor-first wafer with transferred silicon film for transistors on top
idea: Ideal: the capacitor never competes with the transistor for space or heat. Closest: etch and fill deep capacitors in a bulk wafer first, anneal the high-k at >1000 C for its highest-k phase, then Smart-Cut-bond a thin single-crystal Si film on top and build access transistors aligned to the buried capacitor contacts.
why: Facts 1 and 4: capacitor depth is no longer limited by stack height or thermal budget, high-k phase gives Cs gains, and the capacitor module can run in a separate, less advanced line.

title: Photoresist that stays: patternable oxide becomes the device layer
idea: Po: the resist is the product. Use hafnium/zirconium oxo-cluster photoresists that, after exposure and anneal, densify into HfZrO dielectric or hard mask left in place, eliminating the deposit-coat-expose-etch-strip chain for those layers.
why: Process steps and tool count: ~3-4 fewer steps per affected layer, ~5-10% shorter cycle and fewer etch tools.

title: Depreciation-zero heritage-node DRAM consortium for 30-year industrial users
idea: Extreme user: industrial and rail customers who want a part frozen for 30 years. A consortium buys written-off 20-25 nm DRAM fabs, freezes an open process design kit, and runs it at near-zero depreciation for industrial/auto/IoT bits, moving those volumes off leading-edge lines.
why: Capital intensity: depreciation is ~55% of wafer cost, so heritage wafers cost roughly half; frees ~10-15% of leading-edge wafer starts for AI.

title: Eliminate probe cards: contactless whole-wafer optical power and RF readout
idea: Each die carries a small photovoltaic cell and a near-field RF backscatter antenna in the scribe; a high-intensity LED array powers every die on the wafer to run internal BIST, results are read wirelessly in parallel, and the test circuitry is cut off at dicing. DDR/HBM pads are never touched and the product interface is unchanged.
why: Probe cards and ATE channels are a major memory-test capex line; parallel contactless sort tests thousands of dies per shot and leaves hybrid-bond pads pristine.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM with fault-mapped mesh; no dicing or packages
idea: First principle: dicing, packaging and final test are ~15-25% of DRAM cost, and a wafer can stay one device if defects are routed around. Keep the 300 mm wafer as one memory with a reconfigurable on-wafer mesh network and per-tile power gates, so defective or worn tiles are mapped out at test and in the field, and the wafer goes back for tile-level reclaim.
why: Cost per bit and capital (packaging, test, TSVs): ~2 TB per wafer as one repairable unit.

title: Beamlet-failure-tolerant multi-beam direct write for array layers
idea: Combine massively parallel e-beam writers with cell-level error tolerance: ~1% of beamlets may be dead or drifting with no per-beam correction or redundant rescan. The wafer shifts by a sub-pitch offset each pass so a dead beamlet scatters into isolated bad cells rather than whole lines.
why: Per-beamlet reliability and redundant rescans are what keep direct write too slow; relaxing them could raise throughput ~2-3x and make reticle-free, EUV-free array patterning plausible.

title: Dieless memory: deposit arrays directly on the package substrate
idea: Worse: make a die on one substrate, dice it, and bond it onto another (the package). Flip: build low-temperature oxide-TFT memory arrays directly on the glass-core package panel that carries the processor. The result has no die, dicing, bonding or separate test insertion, with memory millimeters from compute.
why: Packaging capital plus data movement (fact 5): die and assembly costs vanish, and short wires cut pJ/bit.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM routes around dead mats and bits
idea: Combine Cerebras-style wafer-scale integration with DRAM: the wafer is never diced but hybrid-bonded whole to a wafer-scale compute or interposer wafer. Mat-level crossbar routing disables dead mats, and a code layer covers 1% cell BER.
why: Removes dicing, per-die packaging, KGD sorting and the HBM TSV/microbump tax, giving ~2-3x bandwidth per edge-mm and ~20% back-end cost avoided (facts 5, 6).

title: Substitute global bitline sensing with local gain transistors from same VCT step
idea: Split each bitline into 16-cell segments; each segment's charge drives the gate of a local gain transistor made in the same vertical-channel-transistor step as the cells (no extra mask), which pulls a ~50 mV current-mode signal onto the global bitline. With a ~1 fF local line, the cell needs only ~1 fF, so the capacitor can be shallow.
why: Constraint: 50 mV global swing instead of ~0.5 V plus 5x smaller cell charge gives ~10-20x less bitline energy per access; facet: capacitor AR from ~70:1 to ~15:1 (fact 1).

title: Self-unzipping polyphthalaldehyde resist enables dry, PAG-free development
idea: Extreme user: thermal-scanning-probe nanolithography, which writes polyphthalaldehyde by local unzipping. Use PPA as a high-resolution resist that depolymerizes to volatile monomer under exposure-triggered heat or weak non-fluorinated acid, so it develops by evaporation with no solvent or developer.
why: PFAS/process: removes PFAS photoacid generators and wet develop/rinse (no pattern collapse at high AR), ~3 fewer steps per litho layer.

title: Idle U.S. silicon-carbide power fabs build hot-proof DRAM transistors
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: 4H-SiC's 3.26 eV bandgap keeps off-state leakage negligible even hot, so build the access transistor (or gain-cell write device) in 200 mm SiC power fabs left underused by the SiC glut, then hybrid-bond a silicon capacitor/periphery wafer on top.
why: Fact 3 and capital: retention of seconds or more at 125 C (refresh ~1000x rarer) using existing U.S. SiC capacity instead of new DRAM fabs; density is limited by ~90 nm SiC litho.

title: Substitute room temperature with 77 K so shallow capacitors suffice
idea: Operate DRAM in liquid nitrogen, where access-transistor leakage drops >10^6, so a 0.5-1 fF capacitor with AR ~10:1 holds data for minutes; subthreshold slope steepens to ~20 mV/dec, letting array voltages fall to ~0.5 V while bitline resistance drops ~5x.
why: Constraint: 5x smaller C and 2x lower V give ~20x lower array energy per access (net ~10x after large-plant LN2 cooling overhead); facet: eliminates HAR capacitor etch and support meshes (facts 1 and 4).

title: Roll-to-roll memory tape on stainless steel foil
idea: Worse: process memory one rigid wafer at a time through vacuum load locks. Flip: run 30 um stainless-steel foil, planarized with spin-on glass, through roll-to-roll UV nanoimprint, atmospheric deposition and sputter zones to make cell layers continuously, then cut and stack the tape into blocks.
why: Throughput/capital: continuous web at meters/min, tool cost per m2 ~10-50x below wafer fabs, abundant U.S.-made steel.

title: Sapphire miscut step-bunches template sub-10nm wordlines without lithography
idea: Worse: print every line with a photon. Flip: anneal vicinal c-plane sapphire until its atomic steps bunch into a periodic 8-20 nm terrace grating, then decorate the step edges by step-flow selective nucleation of metal or oxide semiconductor. Parallel wordlines then form across the whole substrate.
why: Litho (fact 4): a sub-EUV-pitch wordline layer at zero mask cost, on sapphire grown without quartz crucibles.

title: Eliminate greenfield fabs: convert shuttered 300 mm shells to DUV DDR4/DDR5
idea: Re-equip idle or shuttered US 300 mm shells with refurbished DUV-era DRAM tools to make 1x-nm DDR4, DDR5 and LPDDR4 for industrial, auto and PC markets, freeing leading-edge capacity for HBM. Parts are standard JEDEC devices.
why: Capital and time: ~1/3 the capex and ~1/2 the time of a greenfield fab, with no new interface for customers to qualify.

title: Excimer-laser crystallized silicon tiers for monolithic 3D DRAM
idea: Combine LTPS-display line-beam laser crystallization with 3D DRAM: amorphous Si tiers are deposited one at a time over the finished lower tiers, and each is melted and crystallized by a nanosecond laser that heats only the top ~50 nm. This replaces Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattices.
why: Avoids strain-limited epi superlattices and the selective SiGe removal etch, so tier count is not capped by epitaxy and stays within BEOL thermal budget (fact 2).

title: Ultrasonic piezo excitation speeds nanoimprint resist fill several-fold
idea: Effect: piezoelectric ultrasonic excitation (acoustic streaming and shear thinning). A transducer behind the imprint template drives 20-100 kHz vibration that speeds capillary filling of nanoscale cavities and dissolves trapped gas, cutting fill time per field from ~1 s to ~0.2 s. A ~$400k retrofit of a used imprint tool plus a 24-month defect study.
why: Fact 4: NIL throughput (~25 wafers/hour per head) and bubble defects limit it as an EUV substitute; faster fill raises throughput and cuts litho cost per layer.

title: Strategic memory reserve buys gluts, contracts legacy U.S. lines
idea: Po: the government buys RAM like oil. A U.S. strategic DRAM reserve buys bits in price troughs and releases them in shortages, paired with long-term offtake contracts at existing domestic legacy DRAM lines (auto/industrial parts), smoothing the cycle that deters investment.
why: U.S. manufacturability and cyclic underinvestment: steady demand for domestic mature capacity; damps 4x price spikes.

title: Two-bit-per-capacitor DRAM made viable by 1% sensing tolerance
idea: Combine NAND's multi-level-cell sensing with the DRAM capacitor: four charge levels per cell are read by a charge-sharing, two-step successive-approximation sense amp. The scheme historically failed on margin but works once the code absorbs ~1% level misreads.
why: 2x bits per wafer with the same masks, litho and capacitor, roughly halving capital per bit (facts 1, 4).

title: Open-hardware 1990s stepper cloned by U.S. machine shops
idea: Inverts 'litho tools come from two or three vendors'. Publish an open design for a 248 nm, 0.6 NA, 5x-reduction stepper (expired patents, catalog excimer lasers, fused-silica lenses ground by U.S. optics shops) buildable for ~$2-3M each in volume.
why: Removes the scanner chokepoint for every non-critical layer and for spacer/BCP pitch-multiplied flows; creates a domestic tool base.

title: Ship imperfect dies with burned-in defect maps for OS remapping
idea: Worse: scrap every die that still fails after the repair fuses run out. Flip: sell dies with residual bad rows. An on-die eFuse defect map is read at boot, and the kernel or CXL controller excludes those pages (badblocks for RAM), creating a priced-per-good-GB 'capacity-certified' grade.
why: Throughput/yield: effective yield on large HBM/DDR5 dies rises from ~75% to ~95%, about 15-25% more sellable bits per wafer with no new tools.

title: Grayscale multi-tone EUV exposure defines via and line together
idea: Combine grayscale lithography from micro-optics with a dose-to-depth metal-oxide resist. A three-level attenuated reticle gives contacts full dose and lines half dose, so the resist develops a two-depth relief that transfers via plus trench in one etch.
why: Halves EUV exposures for paired via/line levels in the bitline and periphery metals, saving ~$150-250 per wafer per pass avoided (fact 4).

title: Warehouse fab: sealed tool pods replace the ballroom cleanroom
idea: Shrink the controlled environment from building scale (ISO 3-5 ballroom with massive HVAC) to the cubic metre around each wafer: every tool sits in a sealed N2 mini-environment linked by enclosed overhead wafer tubes, so the shell is an ordinary warehouse.
why: Cleanroom construction and HVAC are ~20-30% of fab capex and a large energy load; could save $2-4B on a $15B fab and about a year of build time.

title: Electrohydrodynamic jet printing of maskless periphery wiring
idea: Minify the mask count of interconnect layers to zero: multi-nozzle EHD jets print sub-100 nm silver/copper lines for periphery routing straight from CAD, so every wafer can carry custom wiring or repair routes.
why: Masks and BEOL capital: removes metal masks and the litho-etch loop for those levels; gives instant design iteration.

title: Eliminate ion implantation: junctions set by in-situ doped epitaxy and work functions
idea: Form access-transistor and periphery source/drains by selective in-situ doped epitaxy and set thresholds with gate-metal work-function stacks and dipole layers, so the flow needs no implanter and no implant masks.
why: Removes ~8-12 non-critical masks plus implanters and activation anneals, shortening cycle time ~10% and lowering tool capex; also removes random dopant fluctuation from the leakage tail.

title: Self-limiting oxidation carves 10 nm channels from 180 nm lines
idea: Inverts 'channel width is printed'. Pattern 180 nm Si lines and use stress-retarded thermal oxidation, which self-limits as the core shrinks, to thin them to uniform ~10 nm wires in a 1990s furnace; strip and wrap with gate for gate-all-around access transistors.
why: Thin all-around channels tighten the leakage tail (fact 3) and cut refresh; sub-litho channels from a furnace, though cell pitch stays litho-bound.

title: S: in-tunnel sulfurization converts Mo into lateral MoS2 access channels
idea: Inside the lateral tunnels of a 3D-DRAM stack, ALD a few-angstrom Mo or MoO3 film around a pre-formed gate, then flow H2S or sulfur vapor so it converts in place to MoS2, giving an atomically thin lateral access transistor exactly where 2D-material transfer is impossible.
why: Facts 2 and 3: gas-phase conversion reaches deep lateral cavities, and MoS2's wide gap shrinks the leakage tail to extend refresh intervals.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM hybrid-bonded whole onto wafer-scale AI engines
idea: Extreme user: wafer-scale AI processors that starve for on-wafer memory. Fabricate a full DRAM wafer with row/column redundancy and route-around and hybrid-bond it face-to-face to a logic wafer, skipping dicing, packaging, TSVs and per-die test.
why: HBM tax/capital: removes HBM packaging, TSV area and stack-yield loss; ~10x bandwidth per watt and no interposer.

title: Perovskite-solar ink chemistry for k-70 capacitor dielectrics
idea: Borrowed from perovskite-solar labs, which make films by spin-coating inks and low-temperature anneals: infiltrate Ba-Sr-Ti alkoxide inks into storage holes with supercritical-CO2 assist, then crystallize the BST (k 70-150) by flash-lamp photonic curing, all in a glovebox-scale line a 10-person team can run.
why: Fact 1: a k jump allows AR ~50 instead of 115 without a $5M ALD tool; conformal infiltration into 20 nm holes and leakage at nm thickness are high risk.

title: OLED fine-metal-mask evaporation: resistless shadow patterning of thick metals
idea: Borrowed from OLED fabs, which pattern pixels by evaporating through fine metal masks with no photoresist: pattern DRAM's coarse top-metal, power grid and redistribution layers (>3 um lines) by depositing through reusable Invar shadow masks on a small-team-built aligner, deleting coat, expose, develop, etch and strip for those levels.
why: Fact 4: removes 3-5 litho loops per wafer on non-critical layers, roughly 5-8% of process steps and their tools.

title: Laminated foil stack: 100 printed sheets per block
idea: Magnify tiers through lamination instead of deposition: print memory on 10 um foils, laminate 100 foils into a 1 mm block, and connect them through laser-drilled, printed-fill vertical edge vias.
why: 3D DRAM tier problem: 100 tiers with no tier-by-tier deposition yield compounding, because each foil is tested before lamination.

title: Auto-parts remanufacturing line rebins harvested server DRAM into CXL pools
idea: Run a reman line: robots strip DIMMs from retired servers, packages are desoldered, X-ray screened, burned in and retention-binned, then reballed onto CXL Type-3 expander boards whose controller sets refresh and ECC per bin.
why: Supply without fabs: usable capacity at ~10-20% of new-DRAM cost with zero wafer starts; capital is handlers and testers, not fabs.

title: Mist-CVD gallium oxide write transistors, deposited without vacuum
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years and with no vacuum deposition tools: grow alpha-Ga2O3 (~4.9 eV bandgap) channels by ultrasonic mist CVD at atmospheric pressure and ~400 C over the CMOS periphery, giving a gain-cell write transistor whose projected leakage stays in the sub-aA range even hot.
why: Fact 3: refresh-free retention at 125 C; capital: mist-CVD tools cost ~1/10 of ALD/PVD clusters and are BEOL-compatible.

title: Direct nanoimprint of sol-gel high-k: pattern the dielectric itself
idea: Box: imprinted metal-oxide charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x thermal imprint of a ZrO2/HfO2 sol-gel with a PDMS replica of an EBL master. The functional film acts as the resist: imprinting forms corrugated 3D capacitor shapes and a cure converts it to oxide, deleting the resist-etch-strip sequence.
why: Collapses ~4 steps per layer and avoids high-AR plasma etch for capacitor area enhancement using a university imprint press; risk is shrinkage cracking and leakage of solution-derived oxide.

title: Origami membrane: one hinge mask folds memory panels into tiers
idea: Fabricate a <=300 nm oxide-semiconductor memory membrane over a sacrificial film and use the one added mask to place SiN/Cr bilayer stress hinges between panels; on release, hinges fold the membrane accordion-style into 4-8 stacked panels over the periphery, with hinge traces as vertical interconnect.
why: Facts 2 and 6: multi-tier memory from one planar flow plus one mask and no TSVs; footprint density x4-8.

title: Lease bit-hours with guaranteed take-back of every module
idea: First principle: memory's value is the service (bit-hours), not ownership, and ownership strands bits in idle or retired machines. Sell DRAM as a lease priced per GB-month with contractual take-back, embedded serial and health logs, and redeployment of returned modules into lower-tier fleets.
why: Usable supply: ~1.5-2x more lifetime use per fabricated bit; recurring revenue finances fabs.

title: Inductive coil links stack trailing DRAM dies without TSVs
idea: Po: the stack is wireless. Stack thinned DRAM dies from existing lines and pass data vertically through near-field inductive coils drawn in standard top metal (no TSV etch, fill or reveal), with power delivered by edge wire bonds or a few large vias.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): removes the TSV module and much of its area/yield tax, enabling HBM-like stacks from trailing fabs at ~1 pJ/bit.

title: Periphery on legacy 200 mm US fabs, bonded to array
idea: Minify what needs a leading-edge fab to only the dense cell array; make the 49% periphery (sense amps, decoders, I/O) on underused 200/300 mm mature-node US fabs, then wafer-to-wafer hybrid bond the two.
why: Periphery die area and capital: frees ~half of expensive DRAM wafer area for bits (~1.8x density per DRAM wafer) and reuses depreciated US fabs for the logic half.

title: Block-copolymer holes hardened by sequential infiltration for deep etch
idea: Box: Si trench charge x planar access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x PS-b-PMMA cylinder graphoepitaxy in EBL-written guides, ALD sequential infiltration (TMA/H2O) turning PMMA into an AlOx hardmask, then cryo-DRIE. This yields 20-30 nm holes at ~40 nm pitch with a self-made inorganic mask robust enough for AR >30 silicon etch.
why: EUV-free sub-40 nm hole arrays (fact 4) from a spin coater, ALD and ICP; risk is DSA defectivity (needs ~1/cm2) and placement error.

title: Eliminate the fab's lithography: DNA-origami templated nanoscale memory assembly
idea: DNA origami tiles bind to a coarse DUV-patterned wafer and place carbon-nanotube transistors and metal-oxide nanoparticle capacitors with ~5 nm precision, after which ALD locks and metallizes the assembly; the cell layout is coded in DNA sequence, not masks.
why: Ultimate litho elimination: sub-10 nm cells from a fab of wet benches, coarse litho and ALD; speculative, but would cut capital per bit by >10x.

title: Tungsten-free retrofit: molybdenum precursors in existing CVD chambers
idea: Po: memory needs no tungsten. Swap WF6 for MoO2Cl2/MoCl5 precursors in existing W CVD/ALD chambers (minor heater and delivery changes) for buried wordlines, contacts and plugs, gaining lower resistance in narrow lines.
why: Scarce resource (China ~80% of tungsten): removes W dependence with tool retrofits, no new fab; lower wordline RC as a bonus.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access device with true zero off-leakage
idea: Box: MIM charge x vertical NEMS contact relay (TiN beam over an ALD sacrificial gap) x voltage sense amp x BEOL x Si x three-mask surface micromachining plus vapor-HF release. An open relay passes no current, so the leakage tail (fact 3) and refresh vanish, and the device needs only sputter, ALD and release tools.
why: Kills refresh's 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss with crude lithography; risk is contact endurance (need >1e15 cycles, best ~1e10-1e12) and ns switching needing sub-100 nm beams.

title: Military logistician: containerized sub-400 C memory micro-fabs shipped to sites
idea: A logistician ships capability in boxes. Because a <=400 C flow needs no furnaces, epi or implanters, pack a complete memory-tier line (sputter, PE-ALD, imprint stepper, etch, wet clean, metrology) into ~20 mini-environment 40-ft containers that deploy beside packaging plants or logic fabs and add tiers to purchased CMOS wafers.
why: Mass-produced modules could bring capex to ~$200-500M per 10k wafers/month, deploy in 6-12 months and spread U.S. manufacturing. Risks: contamination control and yield at container scale.

title: Angled ion beams stretch features, deleting cut masks
idea: Po: the etcher does the lithography. Add tilted, directional ion-beam pattern-shaping chambers to existing etch bays so one exposure's holes are elongated or trimmed in a chosen direction, merging contacts or cutting lines without a second litho-etch pass.
why: Mask count and litho time in trailing fabs: removes ~1 litho-etch pair on 3-5 layers, ~10% fewer process steps.

title: MLCC-style laminated capacitor: deposit plates, don't etch towers
idea: First principle: capacitance needs electrode area, which can come from many thin horizontal plates, as in a multilayer ceramic capacitor, instead of one tall vertical tower. Deposit 30 alternating TiN/high-k layers as blankets, punch one shallow hole per cell, and use selective lateral recess plus side contacts to tie odd plates to the storage node and even plates to the plate line.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): area comes from the number of depositions, which is cheap and AR-free; 5+ fF with hole AR <20:1.

title: Hard-disk patterned-media trick: copolymer density multiplication for templates
idea: Copy the HDD bit-patterned-media playbook: e-beam writes only a sparse guide lattice at 2-3x the final pitch, a PS-b-PMMA or high-chi block copolymer fills in the hexagonal lattice by directed self-assembly, and the rectified pattern is etched into the NIL or mask master.
why: Template and mask mastering cost (fact 4): e-beam write time falls by the square of the multiplication factor (4-9x), so template refresh is cheap; the native hexagonal lattice matches the honeycomb 6F2 capacitor layout.

title: Vacuum-free spatial ALD heads for capacitor dielectrics
idea: Po: the fab runs at room pressure. Replace vacuum ALD chambers with atmospheric spatial ALD: wafers rotate under gas-bearing heads with alternating precursor zones, depositing ZrO2/HfO2 and TiN ~10x faster with no load locks or pumps.
why: Tool cost and throughput in the capacitor module: ~3-5x lower cost per wafer pass and lower energy.

title: Pattern once, select forever: permanent scaffold lattice
idea: Reverse 'one mask per layer': define one master dielectric grid by double spacer patterning at the very start and keep it as a permanent scaffold; every later layer only fills or opens grid cells, chosen with coarse i-line block masks.
why: Critical-mask count drops from ~20+ to ~2 DUV, the rest on i-line; overlay is set by the scaffold, not the scanner; no EUV.

title: Sacrificial-polymer air gaps between bitlines, no extra mask
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: fill bitline gaps with a thermally decomposable polymer, cap it with porous SiCN and bake at ~400 C so it evaporates through the cap, leaving rigid air gaps that stay stable at 125 C.
why: Facts 1 and 3: bitline capacitance -30-40% raises sense signal, so the Cs needed for hot retention needs ~30% less capacitor height and no added mask.

title: Nanosolar's non-vacuum dream fixed for memory: an atmospheric-pressure fab
idea: Nanosolar and spatial-ALD solar startups died because non-vacuum films lost on efficiency to cheap crystalline silicon. Memory arrays do not need photovoltaic-grade films, so build a fab with no vacuum chambers: damascene electroplated lines, spin-on and atmospheric spatial-ALD dielectrics, anodized memory oxide, imprint patterning, and only periphery chiplets bought from a conventional fab.
why: Meets 100x with stacked decks: vacuum PVD/CVD/etch is ~40% of fab capex and atmospheric tools are ~5-10x cheaper and faster; est. ~$0.1/GB. Trades: film quality, defect density, coarser features.

title: Octuple spacer patterning from KrF-printed mandrels
idea: Reverse 'print at the final pitch': print fat mandrels at ~160 nm pitch with KrF and multiply them 8x through three nested ALD spacer cycles (SAOP), reaching ~20 nm pitch on the array.
why: No EUV and no ArF immersion needed for the array; KrF tools cost about 1/10 of ArFi and 1/30 of EUV, trading litho for cheap deposition and etch.

title: Mux-in-array, sense-out-of-array: oxide-mux array die bonded at micron pitch
idea: Box: Si capacitor charge x BCAT x sense amps moved to a separate logic die x wafer-to-wafer hybrid bond at 1 um pitch x Si x array die fabbed with array plus BEOL IGZO 1:32 bitline multiplexers only. Because bonding cannot reach 30 nm bitline pitch, each bond pad serves 32 bitlines through an oxide-transistor mux, while sense amps, decoders and I/O come from a cheap mature-node logic wafer.
why: Periphery takes ~49% of the die (fact 7): array wafer sheds ~15-20 periphery masks and each DRAM-fab wafer carries ~1.6-1.9x more bits; risk is mux charge-sharing eroding sense margin.

title: Minify the fab: half-inch wafer micro-fabs for distributed DRAM
idea: Minify the wafer to 12.5 mm and the tool to a desk-sized, cleanroom-free unit (Minimal-Fab style sealed shuttle), then run a simple gain-cell DRAM flow in hundreds of $5M micro-fabs placed next to data centers instead of one $15B megafab.
why: Capital intensity and time-to-capacity: capacity can be added in $5M increments in months, not $15B in 4 years; US manufacturability through many small sites.

title: Display-fab memory: stacked oxide-TFT DRAM on Gen-8.5 glass
idea: Constraint: no silicon wafers at all. Repurpose idle Gen-8.5 LCD/OLED backplane lines to build 1T1C capacity memory at ~1 um rules on 5.5 m2 glass, about 100 GB per TFT tier and 8 stacked tiers per panel, sliced into CXL capacity modules with ~200 ns access.
why: Glass area costs ~100x less than silicon and the capex is stranded and depreciated; target <$2/GB capacity tier with zero crucible quartz and no EUV.

title: Ar: gas-cluster ion beam planarization replaces slurry CMP
idea: Planarize dielectric and metal overburden with argon gas-cluster ion beams whose lateral sputtering smooths high spots, using in-line height maps to dose locally; no slurry, pads or post-CMP scrub.
why: Water: CMP plus post-CMP clean uses ~10-20% of fab UPW; GCIB cuts that module ~100% and removes slurry consumables. Throughput is the risk.

title: Stainless-steel self-passivation: copper-manganese self-forming barriers
idea: Stainless steel protects itself as chromium segregates into a thin oxide; use a Cu-Mn alloy seed so on anneal Mn migrates to the dielectric and forms a ~2 nm MnSixOy barrier, eliminating the TaN/Ta barrier PVD steps in DRAM copper wiring.
why: Ta-free (constraint) with fewer steps (fact 4): removes 2 PVD steps per metal level and frees 3-5 nm of line width for copper, lowering periphery RC (fact 7).

title: Tantalum-capacitor anodic forming grows high-k dielectric in a beaker
idea: Borrowed from tantalum and niobium electrolytic capacitors, which 'form' their dielectric by anodizing porous metal at a set voltage, giving perfectly conformal oxide at ~1.5-2 nm/V: line storage holes with Nb or Ti, anodize at 2-4 V in a wafer-scale electrolyte cell a 10-person team can build, self-limiting Nb2O5/TiO2 (k 40-80) to exact thickness, then fill the top electrode.
why: Fact 1 and capex: conformality does not depend on aspect ratio, the tool is a ~$200k plating-style cell, and k 40-80 approaches the k~70 target; leakage of anodic films is the risk.

title: Rajchman laminated ferrite memory built on MLCC production lines
idea: Revive Jan Rajchman's 1960s RCA laminated-ferrite memory, where conductors were screen-printed between ferrite green sheets and co-fired into a solid block, on today's MLCC lines that already stack ~1,000 thin tape layers: X and Y conductors on alternate NiZn-ferrite sheets, laser-punched vias for layer selection, all fired in air. Each conductor crossing is a ferrite bit switched by coincident current.
why: Capital, scarcity and the constraint: MLCC lines make trillions of parts a year with no litho, no vacuum and no rare gas; 1,000 layers at ~1 Mb/cm2 each give ~1 Gb per cm2 of footprint at materials cost of cents. Risks are ferrite switching speed (tens of ns at small volumes) and drive current.

title: Havana mechanic: revive mothballed fabs and stack proven old-node dies
idea: Havana mechanics keep 1950s cars running for decades. Restart idle, fully depreciated 300 mm 2x-nm DRAM and logic lines, including U.S. ones, to make proven 8 Gb DDR4-class dies, then hybrid-bond 8-16 of them into high-capacity stacks for CXL capacity memory, where bandwidth matters less.
why: Capex per GB near zero with mature yields, and it frees leading-edge wafers for HBM; bits per wafer are ~2-3x worse, but capital is ~1/10. Risks: power per bit and stacking cost.

title: DRAM in the metal layers of any logic wafer
idea: Magnify where memory can be made: build a low-temperature (<400 C) gain-cell DRAM inside the BEOL interconnect stack of foundry logic wafers as two extra metal levels, so no dedicated DRAM fab is needed.
why: Capital intensity: piggybacks on existing logic fab capacity worldwide, including US foundries; incremental cost is a few masks rather than a new $15B fab.

title: Rack-level remapping lets fabs ship dies without laser repair
idea: Move repair up from the die (fuse banks, spare rows, laser repair station) to the rack: each die ships with an OTP defect map and the CXL memory-pool controller remaps around bad 1 MB regions in its page tables, accepting dies with up to ~3% dead capacity.
why: Eliminates laser-repair tools and most redundancy area (~3-5% of die), shortens test, and lifts effective yield 10-20 points on a new node (Facts 4, 7).

title: Gen-8.6 display-glass oxide-TFT DRAM for capacity-hungry AI tiers
idea: Extreme user: AI clusters that need petabytes of warm memory and tolerate relaxed density. Build IGZO-TFT 1T1C arrays on 2.2x2.5 m display glass in idle Gen-8.6 LCD/OLED fabs (each panel ~70x a 300 mm wafer area) with the sense amps on attached silicon chiplets.
why: Capital: display fabs are overbuilt and depreciated; area cost ~1/50 of 300 mm silicon offsets the 50-100x lower density, giving a cheap capacity tier with zero new fab construction.

title: Chlorine-etchable alumina interlayer stack replaces fluorocarbon oxide etch
idea: Extreme user: 200C downhole tools that need high thermal conductivity. Swap SiO2/SiN interlayer, spacer and support films for Al2O3, AlN and ZrO2 stacks that etch cleanly in BCl3/Cl2 plasma and atomic-layer etch, removing every fluorocarbon oxide-etch step.
why: Process/PFAS: drops the C4F6/C4F8 etch-gas supply and the abatement plant; Al2O3/AlN's ~10x higher thermal conductivity cools dense arrays.

title: Xylem transpiration draws metal nanoink void-free into deep capacitor holes
idea: Trees lift sap by evaporation through nanoporous leaf surfaces; cap the wafer with a nanoporous evaporation membrane so solvent leaves only through the top, pulling a Ru or Mo nanoparticle ink into 60:1 storage-node holes without trapped voids, then sinter at ~350 C.
why: Replaces CVD TiN/W electrode fill, removing tungsten (China ~80%) and costly CVD fill tools; wet-bench fill at est. 1/5 tool cost (fact 1, resources).

title: Maskless periphery: multi-beam e-beam writes the logic, not masks
idea: Reverse which part gets masks: the regular array uses cheap periodic patterning, while the irregular periphery (~49% of die) is direct-written by massively parallel multi-beam e-beam, so no periphery reticles exist.
why: Removes ~15-25 periphery masks per product ($ tens of M) and EUV for logic-like layers; enables quick low-volume SKUs.

title: Rolling film masks printed for pennies
idea: Minify mask cost from ~$300k to under $100 by roll-printing flexible photomasks and using rolling near-field contact lithography to pattern non-critical DRAM layers.
why: Masks: disposable printed masks for periphery and BEOL layers cut mask-set spend and lead time.

title: Fiddlehead roll-up: printed foil memory coiled a hundred turns
idea: Ferns pack a large frond into a tight coil; roll-to-roll imprint a 2T0C oxide-TFT memory array on 2 um polyimide foil at ~1 um rules (processing cost per m2 ~1/100 of a silicon wafer), route bus lines to one edge, then wind the foil 100+ turns into a dense cylinder whose edge contacts bond to a CMOS controller.
why: Low planar density is offset by 100x volumetric stacking: ~10x bits per board footprint at equal or lower cost per bit, using printing lines instead of EUV fabs (fact 4).

title: Kilometer-scale web: printed gain-cell memory sheets
idea: Magnify the substrate to a 1 m-wide polyimide web moving at 10 m/min, printing oxide 2T gain cells at 20 um2 per bit (~6 GB per m2), used as a capacity tier behind an SRAM/DRAM cache.
why: Capital intensity: a roll-to-roll line costs ~$20-50M; at ~$20/m2 this targets a few dollars per GB with zero EUV.

title: C: diamond-armored nanoimprint templates for repetitive array layers
idea: Coat nanoimprint replica templates with a thin conformal CVD-diamond skin so they survive >10x more imprints and resist particle damage, then use step-and-repeat nanoimprint for the 3-4 most periodic array layers (holes, lines) instead of EUV.
why: Fact 4: NIL tools cost ~1/5-1/10 of EUV in capital and energy; template wear and defects are NIL's blocker for DRAM, which diamond's hardness and inertness attack.

title: Self-limiting oxidation thins channels until quantum confinement widens bandgap
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: oxidize silicon pillars where stress makes oxidation stop at a ~2 nm core, so quantum confinement lifts the effective bandgap to ~1.6-2 eV; the final channel size is set by chemistry, not lithography.
why: Fact 3: hot leakage ~100x lower; fact 4: removes a critical trim litho/etch step; variability is the main risk.

title: Retrofit idle web presses into printed-memory lines
idea: Minify fab capex to ~$20M per line by converting idle US newspaper and packaging web presses into memory lines, adding laminar-flow tunnels around the web path and inline photonic/laser stations.
why: US manufacturability and capital: reuses US industrial plants and skilled press workforce; capacity added in months.

title: Substitute monolithic DRAM die with array wafer bonded to logic periphery
idea: Fabricate the cell array on an array-only wafer (no periphery transistors and no dual/triple gate-oxide modules, roughly half the masks) and the sense amps, decoders and I/O on a 28-16 nm logic wafer, then hybrid bond the two wafer-to-wafer at ~1 um pitch.
why: Facts 7 and 4: periphery (~49% of die) moves under the array to existing logic foundries; die area -30-40% and array-wafer process steps about -35%.

title: Wafer-scale MoS2 epitaxy on sapphire for stackable access transistors
idea: Worse: insist that the access transistor be bulk crystalline silicon. Flip: grow single-crystal monolayer MoS2 by MOCVD on step-engineered sapphire and stack transistor layers monolithically at <400 C. The 1.8 eV gap and 0.7 nm body give sub-fA off-current and atomically thin tiers.
why: 3D DRAM tier pitch shrinks ~5x versus Si/SiGe epi, and the leakage tail falls (fact 3).

title: Space-SOI-inspired patterned oxygen implant replaces trench isolation
idea: Extreme user: radiation-hard space chips built on SIMOX silicon-on-insulator. Form cell isolation by masked high-dose O+ implantation and anneal, growing buried and lateral oxide islands in place of STI etch, oxide fill, CMP and HF deglaze.
why: Process/PFAS: removes ~8-10 steps of the STI module and every HF touch on it; also gives buried oxide that cuts junction leakage.

title: Cleaved mica substrates give atomic flatness without CMP
idea: Worse: add dozens of CMP steps and ceria slurry to flatten each layer. Flip: start on cleaved muscovite mica, atomically flat over cm2. Grow oxide-semiconductor and high-k films by van der Waals epitaxy, and keep later tiers flat by vdW-bonded transfer instead of polishing.
why: Process steps: removes ~10-20% of CMP steps and their ceria consumables, on an abundant U.S.-mined substrate.

title: Four-level gain cells double bits without a lithography node
idea: Ideal: more bits from the same pattern. Closest: store four charge levels on the read-transistor gate of a capacitorless gain cell, exploiting its non-destructive current read with a time-to-threshold sensing ADC per sub-array, and refresh only the inner levels that drift first.
why: Fact 4: 2 bits/cell equals several 10-20% node shrinks with zero new tools or masks.

title: Programmable photomask for periphery layers
idea: Minify mask-set cost to zero for non-critical layers by exposing through a 193 nm-compatible spatial light modulator (micromirror array) that reprograms its pattern per layer and per product.
why: Masks: a DRAM mask set costs millions of dollars; periphery variants and test chips become free to iterate.

title: In-die reliability sensors finish qualification in weeks, not quarters
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: embed TDDB, BTI, EM and retention monitor arrays in every die and calibrate a physics-of-failure model at 175 C, replacing lot-by-lot 1000-hour high-temperature operating life tests with continuous, data-driven qualification.
why: Capital and time: cuts 4-6 months from each new fab or node ramp, so capital earns revenue sooner while proving the 10-year life.

title: K: ion-exchanged glass panels replace silicon HBM interposers
idea: Build HBM interposers on 510x515 mm thin glass panels toughened by K+/Na+ ion exchange, laser-drill through-glass vias, and pattern redistribution layers with panel-class tools instead of a 300 mm silicon interposer line.
why: Fact 6 (HBM TSV tax): a panel carries ~4x the area of a 300 mm wafer on cheaper tools; low-loss glass also lowers I/O energy.

title: Rework-orthogonal layer stack: strip and redo any failed step
idea: First principle: wafers are scrapped because removing a bad layer damages the layers beneath. Give each pair of adjacent layers an etchant with >1000:1 selectivity (for example, thin Ge-rich sacrificial interlayers under metals that dissolve in H2O2), so any misprocessed module can be stripped and redeposited, extending rework loops from litho to every module.
why: Capital per good wafer: 2-5% line-yield loss on ~$15k wafers becomes rework; the flow is repairable by design.

title: Electrochemically regenerated wet chemistry: etchants as closed loops
idea: First principle: in most cleans the oxidant is consumed but the acid matrix is not. Regenerate sulfuric-peroxide (SPM) on site as electrochemical persulfate, recover HF/HNO3 by membrane distillation, and electrowin dissolved metals, so wet benches run closed-loop.
why: Water, chemicals and opex: ~70% less chemical purchase and much less UPW; eases U.S. permitting.

title: Shadow deposition: existing topography replaces the next mask
idea: Reverse etch-to-define into deposit-to-define: tilt the wafer and evaporate or sputter at grazing angles so the tall lines already on the wafer shadow precise gaps, forming self-aligned contacts and gate offsets with no litho step.
why: Replaces 1-2 critical DUV/EUV layers with a cheap directional deposition tool; overlay errors go to zero because shadowing is self-aligned.

title: Float-line continuous fab: capacitor module never leaves vacuum
idea: Replace the job-shop flow (500+ FOUP moves) with a linear vacuum line like a float-glass or coil-coating line for the capacitor module: mold deposition, HAR etch, clean, ALD electrode, high-k, top electrode and anneal stations chained wafer-by-wafer with in-line metrology at one takt time.
why: Throughput/capital: ~3-4x shorter module cycle time, less WIP capital and queue-time defects, cleanroom only around the line; ~20-30% lower module cost.

title: Hydrogen-sink liners stabilize oxide-semiconductor cells at 125 C
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: a same-chamber ALD sandwich of AlOx barrier plus Ti/TiOx absorber islands traps hydrogen that would otherwise diffuse into the oxide channel and turn it conductive, so standard hydrogen-rich SiN passivation and forming-gas anneals stay in the flow.
why: Fact 3 and capital: keeps BEOL oxide-channel memory stable for a decade at 125 C without special hydrogen-free tools or materials.

title: Jeweler's plating bath: tungsten-free electroless cobalt or ruthenium wordlines
idea: A jeweler plates gold in a beaker at 60 C. Replace CVD TiN/W buried and stacked wordlines with seed-activated, bottom-up electroless Co or Ru fill from aqueous baths at <90 C, densified at <=350 C.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 chemistry, swaps ~$5M CVD chambers for wet cells, and lowers line resistance, since Co and Ru scale better than W below 20 nm. Risks: void-free fill and electromigration.

title: Child's toothpaste squeeze: liquid-metal-printed atomically thin oxide channels
idea: A child squeezes toothpaste onto glass. Touch a droplet of low-melting In-Sn or gallium alloy (<160 C) to the wafer and wipe: its self-limiting 1-3 nm oxide skin transfers as a continuous InOx or Ga2O3 channel sheet with no vacuum sputter tool, and a <=300 C anneal sets carrier density.
why: Makes ultra-thin, low-leakage oxide channels for gain cells at ~1% of sputter-tool cost, and thinner channels improve off-state. High risk: uniformity at 300 mm, and metal-droplet residue.

title: Protonic three-terminal transistor holds state as pumped ions
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics treats ions as a working fluid: a gate pulse pumps protons from a hydrogenated reservoir through a solid electrolyte into a WO3 channel, changing its conductance; removing the field freezes the ions, so the state is nonvolatile and read non-destructively through a separate channel path.
why: Zero refresh and non-destructive read (fact 8); BEOL-compatible below ~300 C with sputter/ALD only, so it is capital-light with no EUV; ns-scale protonic switching has been reported, but endurance and hot retention are the risks (facts 3, 4).

title: Na: epitaxial NaCl release layers for single-crystal tier transfer
idea: Grow epitaxial NaCl on a reusable crystalline donor, grow single-crystal oxide channel or ferroelectric films on the salt, bond them to the CMOS wafer and dissolve the salt with a small water mist to release the film; the donor is reused hundreds of times.
why: Facts 2 and 4: high-quality stacked tiers without high-temperature processing on the CMOS wafer and without buying a new single-crystal substrate per tier; donor cost amortized ~100x.

title: Cleanroom inside the carrier, no ballroom fab
idea: Reverse the cleanliness boundary: each wafer moves in a sealed, purged micro-pod that docks directly to tool load ports, so the building only needs ISO-8 air instead of a class-1 ballroom.
why: Fab building and HVAC is ~20-30% of fab capex and much of its energy; a sealed-pod fab cuts shell cost and lead time, and suits modular U.S. sites.

title: Liberty-ship modular DRAM fabs prefabricated in shipyards
idea: Extreme user: a wartime surge economy. Freeze one standard DRAM fab design, prefabricate cleanroom, sub-fab and utility modules in shipyards/factories, and barge them to sites for bolt-together assembly, replicating the same fab 10x the way Liberty ships were built.
why: Capital/time: build time ~4 years to ~18 months; learning-curve savings ~20-30% per fab; repeatable U.S. siting.

title: Turn spare 28-65 nm logic fabs into memory fabs
idea: Inverts 'DRAM must come from DRAM fabs'. Standardize a pure-logic-process 3T gain-cell macro (no capacitor module) with on-die short-interval refresh, sold as CXL/UCIe memory chiplets that any mature-node logic fab can run on its existing flow.
why: Unlocks depreciated capacity in months, not 3-5 years; ~0.1-0.15 Gb/mm2 at 28 nm (~3x less dense) on wafers costing ~1/3, near parity cost per bit for cache/near-memory roles.

title: Flash-lamp photonic curing makes ceramic dielectrics on plastic
idea: Minify thermal budget with millisecond xenon flash pulses that heat only the printed film to ~1000 C, sintering dense oxide dielectrics and conductors on a polymer web without damaging it.
why: Process energy and capital: replaces furnaces and vacuum annealing, enabling quality storage dielectrics at web speed.

title: Eliminate up-front tool capex: pay-per-wafer-pass equipment ownership by vendors
idea: Tool vendors own, install and maintain the equipment in a new US DRAM fab and bill per wafer pass with guaranteed uptime; the memory company carries only the building and labor, and vendors refurbish tools for the next node.
why: Capital intensity (depreciation ~55% of wafer cost): turns fixed cost into variable cost, lowers the entry barrier for new US makers and cuts downturn losses.

title: DRAM on glass: repurpose idle Gen-10.5 display fabs
idea: Inverts 'memory needs a semiconductor fab'. Run 2.9 x 3.4 m display lines to build 8 sequential tiers of low-leakage oxide-TFT 1T1C cells at ~1 um rules, giving ~0.5 TB of slow-tier DRAM-class memory per panel for CXL far memory.
why: A Gen-10.5 panel has ~120x a 300 mm wafer's area on built, under-used capital; competitive per GB only if 8-tier panel cost stays under ~$1,500, so it is a capacity-tier hedge with near-zero new fab capital (fact 4).
